featured.title: 5 ways #LondonHasFallen restored our faith in humanity
featured.subtitle: Farzana Dewan on LinkedIn

slides.title: 5 ways #LondonHasFallen restored our faith in humanity
slides.subtitle: Farzana Dewan on LinkedIn
slides.description: Over the weekend, many took to twitter to campaign against a Muslim winning... wait for it….a ‘democratic election’ as the new Mayor of London. The backlash of tweets with #LondonHasFallen echoed the feelings of many struggling to digest that a Muslim could actually be their Mayor. Has London gone crazy? No, definitely not, the hashtag soon backfired when supporters of Sadiq Khan started a parody of tweets suggesting #Londonhasfallen for unity and hope. For many the reactions have in fact restored faith in humanity and the results were truly inspiring. So what does all this hoo-hah tell us? Unity and hope will always win This election taught us Londoners want diversity and inclusion all around not just in London- and it is so ready for it to be represented by someone who can bring just that. Londoners stand united for inclusion, cooperation and to retain their rich diverse culture and to spread hope. London is about creating opportunities for everyone and anyone who wants to work hard, chase their dreams and to excel in what they do. Thats right #LondonHasSpoken! The rising talent of Muslims In a recent article of People Management magazine I discussed the disparity in UK’s Muslims and senior roles. As we know, no two people are the same and their beliefs,values and ethics will vary depending on factors like culture and environment. Whilst there is still a lot of work left to do till we see more Muslims in senior roles- as a muslim women in the workplace, I have always viewed being a Muslim to be an asset and never felt I had to hide my religious identity. My rich background adds a dimension to any culture and I am happy to talk about it openly because it really is an asset. Frankly to be ‘different’ is a good thing and this message should be replicated in every workplace. What Sadiq Khan reinforced is that religion does not prevent you from progressing in your career. I have seen Muslims in the workplace to be authentic, aspiring and always giving it their all. These qualities mark a true leader and we should be nurturing this. Whilst the Muslim talent pool is on a gradual rise, workplaces can do more to reduce unconscious bias through good recruitment practices and to tap into this hidden talent pool. Your background does not define your future Son of a bus driver V son of a millionaire- this for me is the biggest takeaway from this election- reassuring to know you don’t have to be born rich to reach your dreams. Hard work and grit mixed with the right attitude, passion and hunger for success is enough to take you to places. Stereotyping exists but it doesn’t represent the masses People have taken an interest in Islam but for all the wrong reasons. The media has done a presidential amount of damage in creating an unjust image of Muslims worldwide. If and by the time the misunderstanding has been cleared up, its too late, the damage has been done. The word play with ‘Muslim’ has been a conscious use of connotation for terror and attack. The premature, ill researched and slanderous coverage of Muslims in the media has played with vulnerable minds and handicapped their ability to think. Minds have been unconsciously programmed to think negatively and to categorise all Muslims into one box. But luckily these few don’t represent the way of thinking for the masses. Many have the ability to think for themselves and to form a more rounded educated opinion. Politeness and humbleness will never get old And lastly no one likes a sour loser- don’t be a Paul Golding! Bad mouthing or turning your back to your opponent on their victory speech is never a good look. Express humbleness and congratulate your opponent- you might just gain few new followers! Politics is something that I don’t normally express my opinion on but at a time like this when society gets together to tell us they choose hope over fear and diversity over division is when its worth talking about. No doubt #LondonHasRisen

publications.description: Technology has given chief learning officers the tools to make learning a seamless and integrated part of the work experience. To succeed, CLOs can make several fundamental changes.

publications.title: Reviving the Art of Apprenticeship
publications.description: In a dynamic and rapidly changing environment, professional skill gaps need filling, and formal learning alone won’t do the trick. Scaling the lost art of one-on-one learning can make the difference.

publications.title: Why Cognitive Apprenticeship is new again
publications.description: What was once old is new again – which is why we are discussing Cognitive Apprenticeship with Lisa Christensen, Director of Learning and Development at McKinsey & Company. Jake and Lisa completed a study last year to learn how Covid-19 has impacted learning through apprenticeship. As a result, Lisa went deeper into the field of Cognitive Apprentice to determine how it can make us more efficient and effective (both as the apprentice and teacher) in our everyday interactions. In addition, we discuss traditional apprenticeship vs. cognitive apprenticeship, the methods, techniques to apply the methods, and why it is perceived to be difficult.

publications.title: Intentional Learning: A Fundamental Skills
publications.description: Learning is a skill and considered the most fundamental skills of our time. In this episode, Lisa Christensen (Director of Learning and Development CoE at McKinsey & Company) and Matt Smith (Partner and CLO at McKinsey & Company) join the show to discuss their research on Intentional Learning. The crew discusses the mindsets and skills of intentional learners, why it’s difficult to master and support, and steps you can begin today to unlock intentionality in your career.

volunteering.description:
Kumbo is a small village located at the NW of Cameroon. There is where the effective part of the project took place. The project aimed to provide useful knowledge and easy-to-build green energy solutions to locals. That way three main aspects will be improved:

•	Social through better living conditions.
•	Human through education.
•	Economical through commerce and power generation.

A secondary objective was to raise awareness on the importance of using green power energy sources. The scope was set on Kumbo and nearby villages.

For the three years I coordinated the project at university I was able to strengthen my leadership and managerial skills, achieving all our objectives and expanding participation by a +100% and in projects (from 1 to 4).

Our core area comprised a series of courses that provided useful knowledge to locals. That knowledge covered from hydro electrical power sources to electrical distribution and security passing through many alternative energy sources.

The project was launched by the “Fundación de Ingenieros para el Desarrollo” and collaborates with other entities such as “Manos Unidas” or “Energías sin fronteras”.

I am the Managing Partner of McKinsey and Company's Australia and New Zealand Practice and one of the founders McKinsey's Global Transformation Practice, counselling companies on significant and sustainable business transformation.

As an Associate at McKinsey & Company and a Chicago Booth MBA CO'25, I bring a strong foundation in data-driven approach and client empathy to my work. My education, paired with multi-disciplinary experience, enables me to analyze complex problems and propose actionable strategies that align with business goals.  

My recent role at Nutanix includes contributing to product roadmaps, where I conducted market research and competitive analysis to identify opportunities in the AI and HPC ecosystems and developed AI strategy for Nutanix focusing on partnerships and acquisitions across the GenAI horizontal lifecycle. My experience prior to Chicago Booth spans consulting and analytics at Accenture, fintech strategy at HDFC, and developing language models and researching Ethical AI for Walmart 1B+ catalogue.

I am driven by a commitment to leveraging data-driven insights to inform decisions, foster innovation, and deliver impactful results.

Outside of work, I'm a huge sports fan (Football/Soccer, F1, FPL to name a few) and you can find me in the gym or hiking/doing some kind of adventure sports or trying to be an amateur Gordon Ramsay.

headline: Advisor
about:
I am Norwegian and live in Zürich since 1988. Education wise, I am a lic.oec from University of St. Gall (HSG, graduate in 1983) and an MBA from University of Chicago (Booth School, graduate in 1984). I was 25 years at McKinsey & Co. as a Senior Partner with main focus on the Travel, Transportation and Logistics businesses. Thereafter, I bought the sensor company, Sensonor, when it was bankrupt in 2012 and developed it into a globally success. Sensonor was sold in 2021 to SAFRAN SA. 

McKinsey & Co. is global leader in top management consulting. I joined in 1985 and was elected Partner in 1991 and Senior Partner in 1997. My big passion was for the Travel, Transportion and Logistics industries. We built this into the undisputed global leader in the field and I was the Global Leader of this Industry Practice from 1996 to 2003. My client relationships were with a large number of leading airlines, the world's biggest logistics companies, leading shipping lines, railroads etc. I supported the clients in transforming them in various forms to leading and competitive businesses, e.g. with restructurings, M&A targeting and integrations, functional excellence, governance etc..  Further, we built McKinsey's capability in the field with methods/tools, databanks, resource pools, "points of views", publications and speeches etc.. I left McKinsey & Co. in 2010 and am now Senior Partner "Emiritus".

In 2012, I bought Sensonor AS in Norway with a Swiss Partner.  Sensonor was an iconic company in the sensor industry which went bankrupt in 2012.  We bought the assets soon after the event. Since 2012, I was the Chairman of the company. In, 2013 I took over as CEO and held that role (with some interruptions) until selling in 2021.  Building on globally leading products in high end gyroscopes and IMUs, we built an excellent customer base (leading Silicon Valley customers as well as global defense leaders) and established a world class quality production system. I had great satisfaction from building and leading the team to make this happen (while also maneuvering difficult waters). It was an extremely multifaceted experience, e.g. capital raising, joint ventures, R&D development etc. We had MUSD 3 sales in 2012 and MUSD 21 in sales (with excellent profitability) when we sold (2021). The company was sold to SAFRAN SA, a global leader in the inertial field.

I took great joy in being a Member of The Board of Trustees of Right to Play (an education focussed charity) in Switzerland. I enjoy spending time outdoors; skiing, hiking or playing golf.

experience.description: Providing broad range of support (strategy, cost reductions, sales/growth, M&A; intergrations etc) for clients in most industries. Build up of McKinsey's travel, transportation and logistics practice.
I have a mix of mandates around business/strategy advisory and support in creating the right investor base/structure for clients.

I bought Sensonor out of bankruptcy in 2012 with a Swiss partner. We developed the company into a highly successful global leader and sold it in 2021 to SAFRAN SA. We grew business from MUSD 3 in 2012 to MUSD 21 in 2021 with excellent profitability.

projects.title: Harbor Point: An Examination of Baltimore's Economic Development Policies
projects.description: Harbor Point is a soon to be developed 27 acre mixed-use waterfront development, which will include office buildings, retail, apartment towers, parks, and the regional headquarters of Exelon Corporation.  This $1B project will put the City of Baltimore into a debt totaling around $400M, due to the use of Brownfield Tax Credits, Enterprise Zones, and TIF.  City Council and Mayor Stephanie Rawlings Blake have justified this public expenditure as a means of economic development.  This thesis analyzes the benefit of these programs as tools for job creation and unemployment amelioration.  This is not the first time Baltimore and the State of Maryland have heavily contributed to the financing of a private project, yet the city still struggles with deteriorating neighborhoods and high unemployment.  If the current models of economic development do not yield results then Baltimore must try a new strategy.  This thesis recommends Baltimore think more creatively regarding economic development policy and suggests the theory and policies of other scholars as a way to invoke change.

publications.title: Centered Leadership
publications.description: In this book by Joanna Barsh and Johanne Lavoie, you'll come as close as possible to experiencing the Centered Leadership Program without being there.  At the heart of Centered Leadership lies the practice of self-awareness and choice. The ability of leaders to be mindful and at choice in the moment helps them tap into purpose and vision (Meaning), shift habitual patterns into a learning stance (Framing), create collective relationships (Connecting), step up with intention (Engaging), and sustain transformational growth (Energizing).

publications.title: How Remarkable Women Lead
publications.description:
The Remarkable discoveries about what drives and sustains successful women leaders.

Based on five years of proprietary research, How Remarkable Women Lead speaks to you as no other book has, with its hopeful outlook and unique ideas about success. It's the new "right stuff" of leadership, raising provocative issues such as whether feminine leadership traits (for women and men) are better suited for our fast-changing, hyper-competitive, and increasingly complex world. 

The authors, McKinsey & Company consultants Joanna Barsh and Susie Cranston, establish the links between joy, happiness, and distinctive performance with the groundbreaking model of Centered Leadership. 

The book's personal stories and related insights show you the magic that happens when you put the five elements of Centered Leadership–meaning, framing, connecting, engaging, and energizing–to work. They include:

• How Alondra de la Parra built on her strengths and passions to infuse her life with meaning and make her way in the male-dominated world of orchestra conducting
• How Andrea Jung, the CEO of Avon, avoided a downward spiral when the company turned down by "firing herself" on Friday and re-emerging on Monday as the "new" turnaround CEO
• How Ruth Porat's sponsors at Morgan Stanley not only helped her grow but were also her ballast for coping with difficult personal and professional times
•How Eileen Naughton recovered after losing her dream job, landing on her feet at Google and open to a new leadership opportunity 
• How Julie Coates of Woolworth's Australia makes energy key to her professional success, with reserves for her "second shift" as wife and mother

How Remarkable Women Lead is both profoundly moving and actionable. Woman or man, you'll find yourself in its pages and emerge with a practical plan for breaking through at both work and in life.

headline: McKinsey Partner | Automotive Supplier | Corporate Strategy | Value Creation Transformation (Growth and ROIC) | Portfolio, M&A (diligence to integration), Divestiture | New Venture
topSkills: Business Transformation • Corporate Strategy • Mergers & Acquisitions (M&A) • Due Diligence • New Business Development
about:
I help automotive supplier CEOs, CFOs, and business leaders drive step-change value creation, expanding EBITDA and ROIC while building a durable growth engine.

At McKinsey, and as a Scholar at the McKinsey Center for Future Mobility, I work with Tier 1 and Tier 2 suppliers across the decisions that most directly expand enterprise value: 
1. Margin expansion and performance transformations: commercial opportunities, cost base reset, operating model, footprint, SG&A +E effectiveness, and operational discipline that make gains stick
2. ROIC and cash improvement: working capital, capital allocation, capex effectiveness
3. Growth strategy: where to play, how to win, customer and segment choices, innovation roadmaps, and commercial acceleration
4. M&A end-to-end: diligence, synergy underwriting, integration planning, and post-merger value capture
5. Portfolio moves: divestitures and carve-outs, sell-side diligences, separation planning, and equity story development
6. New business building: adjacency expansion, new business models, and venture build-out from strategy through operating launch

My work is often at the intersection of operational realities with value creation levers, helping leadership teams make confident moves amid electrification, autonomous vehicles, software-defined vehicles, shifting value pools, and changing OEM supplier dynamics.

Before McKinsey, I held strategy and operating roles inside an automotive supplier, leading Lean and cost programs and driving measurable operational improvements. I hold an MBA from Chicago Booth and an MS in Mechanical Engineering.

I’m a McKinsey consultant with a background in engineering, operations, and early-stage investing. I’m passionate about helping organizations align their vision with day-to-day execution. I thrive at the intersection of strategy and implementation, whether it’s driving frontline engagement for a global manufacturer, reimagining operating models for a Fortune 50 energy player, or advising startup founders as they scale. In every role, I focus on translating ambition into measurable results.

My leadership philosophy is rooted in a people-first approach. Whether I’m navigating senior executives through strategic ambiguity or mentoring the next generation, I am committed to lifting as I climb, ensuring that progress is collective, not individual, and believing that the best solutions emerge when everyone has a voice and a seat at the table.

Impact is my guiding principle. Within the firm, I mentor junior consultants and drive inclusion initiatives that build stronger, more resilient teams. Beyond the office, I mentor high school students and advise aspiring MBAs, helping them unlock opportunities at top programs like HBS, Wharton, Chicago Booth, and MIT Sloan. For me, true leadership means investing in others at every level and every stage.

Credentials:
MBA, Harvard Business School; B.E., Chemical & Molecular Engineering, Stony Brook University

Engineer by training, builder at heart, lifelong learner. If you’re passionate about strategy, growth, or mentorship, let’s connect!

experience.description:
National Science Foundation sponsored Research Experience for Undergraduates (REU) Internship
Presented my research at the AIChE National conference in Atlanta, GA in November 2014.
Research Title: Fabrication and Optimization of Deep UV Photonic Crystals
Research Scope: We are investigating different synthetic conditions of highly charged silica nanospheres which we use to create photonic crystal wavelength selecting devices. These photonic crystals consist of a crystalline colloidal array of small (30-45 nm diameter) silica nanospheres which are highly monodisperse in size and charge. The current goal is to optimize the size and charge of the particles in order to improve the diffraction properties of our photonic crystals i.e. strong diffraction with a narrow bandwidth. These particles were functionalized with strongly acidic groups, resulting in a high negative surface charge. This high charge leads to electrostatic repulsion between nanospheres and self-assembly into face centered cubic photonic crystals which Bragg diffract a narrow wavelength region of UV light.
